clue.text: Child loves repeating word for train

indicators.note: repeating says the letters built from child and loves are written out twice in a row

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, and zero looks like the letter O; two loves give two Os

explanation.surface: A youngster keeps saying the nursery word for a railway engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery talk for a steam locomotive imitates the noise of its puffing engine.

clue.text: Like a room, as it were, somewhere in France

definitions.text: Like a room, as it were
definitions.meaning: a jokey adjective formed by adding -y to a word for a room, meaning room-like
a town in the Savoie region of eastern France, known for its vermouth

explanation.definitionFit: Chambery is a French Alpine town, and read as chamber plus -y it jokily means room-like.

clue.text: Second part of Messiah, perhaps, introduces new stars

indicators.note: the second part of a word means only its latter half is kept, the first half being dropped

parts.note: Handel's Messiah is an example of an oratorio, a sacred choral work

explanation.surface: A programme note on the second half of Handel's Messiah featuring fresh star soloists.
explanation.walkthrough: Handel's Messiah is the classic example of the sacred choral form; only the second half of that word is kept before the N goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is a prominent constellation, a named group of stars, the Hunter.

clue.text: Diver may be itching to meet required standards

definitions.meaning: a diver will rise to the surface, and someone itching wants to relieve the itch with the nails: two phrases run together
to reach the expected level of performance

explanation.walkthrough: Read the first half as two phrases: what a diver does at the end of a dive, and what someone itching wants to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for reaching the expected level comes from boxers having to step up to a line marked on the ground.

clue.text: Said to bypass Belgium, it is a kind of motorway

indicators.note: a bypass road goes round a town, so the spoken word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: oral means spoken, said rather than written
B is the international vehicle registration letter for Belgium
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims a ring road skirting Belgium is a type of motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' looks like a homophone signal, but here it is just a synonym for spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital motorway is a ring road that circles a city, such as London's M25.

clue.text: Supplies heavily-scented flowers

definitions.meaning: goods held in reserve, as a shop's inventory
garden plants of the genus Matthiola, prized for their strong clove-like fragrance

explanation.definitionFit: Stocks are both reserves of goods and a fragrant cottage-garden flower.

clue.text: Competent healer working in teetotal accommodation

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked over into a new shape

explanation.surface: A capable doctor is employed at a dry hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the fifteen letters of COMPETENT HEALER; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperance hotel served no alcohol, catering to guests sworn to abstain from drink.

clue.text: Insurance document co-author used to protect books

indicators.note: something used to protect another surrounds it, so the books go inside

parts.note: CO (a prefix meaning joint) plus VERNE, the French author Jules Verne
OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An insurance form whose joint writer uses it as a dust jacket for volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated word splits into a prefix meaning joint and the French novelist Jules Verne; the Old Testament books sit inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover note is a temporary certificate an insurer issues before the full policy is ready.

clue.text: Such wintry weather? Shelter in farm enclosure

indicators.note: in places the shelter inside the farm enclosure

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs on a farm
lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A farmer sheltering from icy weather in the pig pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather full of half-frozen rain falling as ice pellets is a wintry condition.

clue.text: Game boy's a painter

parts.note: RU is rugby union
Ben's, a boy's name with the possessive

explanation.surface: A lad who plays a sport turns out to be an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was the great Flemish Baroque painter.

clue.text: A team should be given award — that goes without saying

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a football or cricket side
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Naturally a side should receive a prize, as everyone knows.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident truth, a statement accepted without needing proof.

clue.text: Book, disgraceful volume that is made into a porn film?

indicators.note: disgraceful suggests the word volume is put into disorder

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A scandalous book adapted into an adult film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disgraceful' rearranges VOLUME into LUEMOV; 'made into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue movie is an old slang term for a pornographic film; the query marks the definition as playful.

clue.text: Lots of food and drink, but not a seat for diners

definitions.text: Lots of food and drink, but not a seat for diners

parts.words: Lots of food and drink, but not a seat for diners
parts.note: the word looks like a lavish feast with a French suffix, but names an upholstered bench along a restaurant wall

explanation.walkthrough: The answer begins with the word for a grand meal, which the clue says it is not: it is the seating.
explanation.definitionFit: A banquette is a long padded bench seat, typically fixed along the wall of a restaurant.

clue.text: Wader goes backwards into water, generally

indicators.note: goes backwards says the run of letters is read from right to left
into points to letters found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A heron-like bird retreats into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'water, generally' read backwards sits the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: Tearful about making denial

indicators.note: about can mean around or roundabout, signalling the letters are turned around and reordered

explanation.surface: Someone weeping while issuing a denial.
explanation.definitionFit: A refutal is an act of refuting, a rebuttal or denial of a claim.

clue.text: The lady's not for burning

parts.note: the title of Christopher Fry's play, reread as describing a woman whose job is to stop fires

explanation.walkthrough: The Lady's Not for Burning is a 1948 verse play by Christopher Fry.
explanation.definitionFit: A female firefighter's role is putting out blazes, so she is against burning.

clue.text: Little boy blue's first time

indicators.note: first says the blue piece comes before the boy

parts.note: the blue is a poetic name for the sea
a son is a little boy

explanation.surface: The nursery rhyme Little Boy Blue's debut.
explanation.definitionFit: A season is a period of time, such as a quarter of the year.

clue.text: Attractive woman wearing red was revolting

indicators.note: wearing means the colour goes round the woman like clothing

parts.note: taken as written
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A beauty dressed in scarlet behaved badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgusting, but here it means rising up.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt is to rise up against authority, as rebels do.

clue.text: High-spirited fellow likely to cause mishap

parts.note: risky means dangerous, liable to lead to accident

explanation.surface: A lively man whose antics are dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky means playful and lively, full of high spirits.

clue.text: Noisy dog salesman reared after getting pay rise

indicators.note: after getting places the salesman's letters after the pay letters
in a down clue rise means the word is written upwards, in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reared means turned up on end, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A loud dog belonging to a salesman who got a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A yapper is a small dog that barks shrilly and constantly.

clue.text: Swimmer almost hit you

annotationWithheld.why: Swimmer almost hit you (7): SOCK (hit) + YE (you) gives SOCKYE, a letter short of SOCKEYE; no sound indicator, so 'almost' cannot be parsed honestly

clue.text: Port rebuilt as new in South Africa

indicators.note: in places the rebuilt letters inside the country abbreviation
rebuilt means the letters are put together again in a different order

explanation.surface: A harbour reconstructed as good as new in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges AS NEW, and the result sits inside the abbreviation for South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a port city on the south coast of Wales.

clue.text: Fur wrap business wound up hasn't succeeded

indicators.note: wound up, in a down clue, means wound upwards, so the whole run is read from the bottom
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, so this asks for that letter to be removed

parts.note: a stole is a wrap worn over the shoulders
CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A fur wrap firm went bust because it failed.
explanation.walkthrough: STOLE without S is TOLE; with CO that is TOLECO, and 'wound up' reverses it all.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocelot is a spotted wild cat whose pelt was prized as fur.

clue.text: Be in debt? When creditor comes round, cringe in fear

indicators.note: comes round means the creditor surrounds the debt

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for creditor
to owe is to be in debt

explanation.surface: A debtor shrinks back in terror when the lender calls.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch or shrink back in fear.

clue.text: Theatre named by Wendy?

parts.note: a toy house for children is named after Wendy in Peter Pan, for whom the Lost Boys built one

explanation.walkthrough: A Wendy house is the British term for a child's play hut, named after Wendy in Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is a theatre, and also a child's toy house, which the British call a Wendy house.

clue.text: Wise person supporting union practice

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the union comes after it

parts.note: a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: A wise man backs a trade union's customs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts SAGE below U in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means customary practice, the habitual way something is done.

clue.text: All-pervasive smell — it is worrying

indicators.note: worrying suggests the letters are troubled and tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: An all-pervading odour is a cause of concern.
explanation.definitionFit: Something limitless has no bounds, extending everywhere without restriction.

clue.text: Way to advertise upcoming programmes

definitions.meaning: to show a preview of coming broadcasts

explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path, and to trail a programme is to promote it in advance.

clue.text: Red wine served by host oddly, in tiny portions

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine

indicators.note: oddly asks for the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: A host serving red wine in miserly measures.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old name for a dark red wine from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenths are small fractions, each one part in ten.

clue.text: Pile of bricks could be the demise of an old film star

parts.note: Clark Gable was a Hollywood star of the 1930s to 1950s
end means death or demise

explanation.surface: A heap of bricks marking the death of a Hollywood legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A gable end is the triangular brick wall at the end of a pitched roof.
